dct:description: 'A binary observation of the presence of snow cover at the measurement location.'@en
rdfs:label: Presence of snow

dct:description: 'Vertical depth of the water that would be obtained if the freshly fallen snow melted completely, which equates to the new snow mass per unit area.'@en
rdfs:label: Water equivalent of snowfall

dct:description: 'The result of all processes adding and removing mass from the glacier at a point on its surface, expressed over a stated period of time'@en
rdfs:label: Glacier mass balance at a point

dct:description: 'The result of all processes adding and removing mass from the glacier at its surface, expressed over a stated period of time and integrated over the entire glacier area'@en
rdfs:label: Glacier-wide mass balance

dct:description: 'The mass added to the glacier at a point on its surface expressed over a stated period of time.'@en
rdfs:label: Surface accumulation at a point

dct:description: 'The mass removed from the glacier at a point on its surface expressed over a stated period of time.'@en
rdfs:label: Surface ablation at a point

dct:description: 'Area enclosed by the projection of the glacier outline onto the surface of an ellipsoid approximating the surface of the Earth or onto a planar horizontal approximation to that ellipsoid. The glacier area excludes nunataks but includes debris-covered parts of the glacier. The glacier outline separates the glacier from unglacierized terrain and from contiguous glaciers.'@en
rdfs:label: Glacier area

dct:description: 'Ground temperature measured in the permafrost.'@en
rdfs:label: Permafrost temperature

dct:description: 'Thickness of the surface layer of the ground that is subject to annual thawing and freezing in areas underlain by permafrost.'@en
rdfs:label: Active layer thickness

dct:description: 'Ratio of the distance covered by a body of water, moving in a specified direction, to the time taken to cover that distance. [Based on ‘velocity’ in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Stream velocity

dct:description: 'Velocity at a given cross-section of a stream, obtained by dividing the discharge by the cross-sectional area of the stream at that section. [Based on 'mean velocity' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Stream mean velocity

dct:description: 'Velocity of a stream at its surface at a given point. [Based on 'surface velocity' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Stream surface velocity

dct:description: 'Difference in the stage of water surface over a short stream reach. [Based on 'water surface slope' in Manual on Stream Gauging (WMO-No. 1044), Volume II. 2010.]'@en
rdfs:label: Water surface slope

dct:description: 'Elevation of the free water surface of a water body relative to a reference datum (synonym: stage, gage height). [Based on 'water level' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Water level

dct:description: 'Flow of a liquid through an unsaturated porous medium, such as that of water in soil under the effect of gravity for a unit time. [Based on 'percolation' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Percolation rate

dct:description: 'Natural or artificial introduction of water into the saturated zone of an aquifer for a unit time. [Based on 'groundwater recharge' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Recharge rate

dct:description: 'Volume of geological formation capable of storing, transmitting and yielding exploitable quantities of water. [Based on 'aquifer' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Aquifer volume

dct:description: 'Property of a porous medium or fractured rock which, according to Darcy's law, relates the specific discharge to the hydraulic gradient. [based on 'hydraulic conductivity' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Hydraulic conductivity

dct:description: 'Rate at which water is transferred through a unit width of an aquifer under a unit hydraulic gradient. [Based on 'transmissivity' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Hydraulic transmissivity

dct:description: 'Ratio of the volume of the interstices in a given sample of a porous medium to the gross volume of the sample, inclusive of voids. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Porosity

dct:description: 'Volume of the void spaces through which water or other fluids can travel in rock or sediment, divided by the total volume of the rock or sediment. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Effective porosity

dct:description: 'Amount of water held in the soil after gravitational water has drained away expressed as a volume percentage. [Based on 'specific retention' and 'field capacity' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Specific retention

dct:description: 'Flow of water through the soil surface into a porous medium for a unit time. [Based on 'infiltration' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Infiltration rate

dct:description: 'Maximum rate at which water can penetrate the soil matrix per unit area under certain conditions. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Infiltration capacity

dct:description: 'Ratio of discharge of a well to drawdown at equilibrium. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Specific capacity (well)

dct:description: 'Ratio of the volume of water which can be drained by gravity from an initially saturated porous medium to the total volume of the porous medium. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Specific yield

dct:description: 'Volume of groundwater flowing through an aquifer per unit time. [Based on International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Groundwater flow

dct:description: '(1) Impounding of water in surface or underground reservoirs for future use. (2) Volume of water stored. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Storage

dct:description: 'The concentration of all dissolved substances in water, usually expressed in milligrams per litre, which would remain as a solid residue after removal of the water. [Manual on Water Quality Monitoring (WMO-No. 680). 1988]'@en
rdfs:label: Total dissolved solids

dct:description: 'The component of an unacidified water sample that is retained by a 0.45-nm membrane filter. [Manual on Water Quality Monitoring (WMO-No. 680). 1988]'@en
rdfs:label: Suspended sediment

dct:description: 'Rate of movement of sediments in a stream at a given cross-section. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Sediment discharge

dct:description: 'Amount (weight, mass or volume) of sediment that moves on or near the streambed by rolling, sliding, or saltating (bed load) transported through a cross-section of a stream per unit time. [Based on 'bed load discharge' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Bed load discharge

dct:description: 'That part of the total transported sediment which is suspended by turbulence in the flowing water for considerable periods of time without contact with the stream bed, moving with almost the same velocity as the flowing water and generally expressed in mass or volume per unit of time. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Suspended sediment load

dct:description: 'Total quantity of sediment passing through a reach, both in suspension and along the bed, excluding the sediment deposited on the bed within the reach. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Total sediment load

dct:description: 'That part of the precipitation which flows on the ground surface (surface runoff) or within the soil (subsurface runoff or interflow) and is generally expressed in mass or volume per unit of time, its equivalent in linear units (as the height of a water layer covering a given area) or as a fraction of precipitation. [Based on International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Runoff

dct:description: 'Ratio of runoff depth to precipitation depth. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Runoff coefficient

dct:description: 'Runoff volume from a drainage basin, divided by its area, in a specified time. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Depth of runoff

dct:description: 'Percentage of water in soil expressed relative to dry-soil weight or by volume.Synonym: water content of soil. [Based on 'soil moisture content' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Soil moisture

dct:description: 'Volume of water in a reservoir between the minimum and maximum water levels under normal operating conditions. Synonyms: usable storage, active storage, available storage capacity. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Live storage

dct:description: 'Volume of a reservoir including dead storage. Synonym: total storage. [Based on 'total storage' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Reservoir storage

dct:description: 'Volume of water contained in a lake at a given water level. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Lake volume

dct:description: 'Amount of suspended sediment (suspended by turbulence for considerable periods of time without contact with the bed) crossing a stream section per unit time.  [Based on 'suspended sediment' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Suspended sediment discharge

dct:description: 'A velocity that is representative of the average stream velocity; often measured in a profile or across the stream or over the water surface. [Based on 'velocity index method' in Manual on Stream Gauging (WMO-No. 1044), Volume II. 2010]'@en
rdfs:label: Stream index velocity

dct:description: 'Surface velocity of a single rock glacier unit.'@en
rdfs:label: Rock glacier velocity

dct:description: 'Ratio of the distance covered by a body of water, moving in a specified direction, to the time taken to cover that distance. [Based on 'velocity' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Stream velocity

dct:description: 'Velocity at a given cross-section of a stream, obtained by dividing the discharge by the cross-sectional area of the stream at that section. [Based on 'mean velocity' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Stream mean velocity

dct:description: 'Velocity of a stream at its surface at a given point. [Based on 'surface velocity' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Stream surface velocity

dct:description: 'Difference in the stage of water surface over a short stream reach. [Based on 'water surface slope' in Manual on Stream Gauging (WMO-No. 1044), Volume II. 2010.]'@en
rdfs:label: Water surface slope

dct:description: 'Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) magnetic and electric field of the three first resonance modes of the Earth (approximately 8 Hz, 14 Hz, 20 Hz).'@en
rdfs:label: Schumann Resonances

dct:description: 'Amount of water present beneath the ground surface per unit area.'@en
rdfs:label: Groundwater (amount per unit area)

dct:description: 'Elevation of the water table or piezometric surface of an aquifer at a certain location and time. [International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Groundwater level

dct:description: 'Area extent of the surface of a lake.'@en
rdfs:label: Lake area

dct:description: 'Elevation of water in an inland body of surface water of significant extent. [Based on 'water level' and 'lake' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Lake level

dct:description: 'Volume of water flowing through a stream (or channel) cross-section per unit time. [Based on 'discharge' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Stream discharge

dct:description: 'Elevation of the free water surface of a water body flowing in an open or closed conduit. [Based on 'water level'and 'stream' in International Glossary of Hydrology (WMO-No. 385). 2012 edition.]'@en
rdfs:label: Stream level

dct:description: ''@en
rdfs:label: Well discharge

dct:description: ''@en
rdfs:label: Breaking action-friction coefficient

dct:description: 'Location of coastlines (Lat/Long)'@en
rdfs:label: Coastlines

dct:description: 'Processed from land surface imagery by assigning identified cluster(s) within a given area to specific classes of objects - Accuracy expressed as number of classes. Actually [ classes-1 ] is used, so that smaller figure corresponds to better performance, as usual.'@en
rdfs:label: Land cover

dct:description: 'Map of land surface heights.'@en
rdfs:label: Land surface topography

dct:description: ''@en
rdfs:label: Runway conditions

dct:description: 'Fraction of an area flood by water.'@en
rdfs:label: Wetland extent

dct:description: ''@en
rdfs:label: Soil heat Flux

dct:description: 'Result of the classification of different types of soil within an area - Accuracy expressed as inverse of the number of classes, so that smaller figures correspond to better performance.'@en
rdfs:label: Soil type

dct:description: 'Fraction of a land area where fire is occurring.'@en
rdfs:label: Fire fractional cover

dct:description: 'Power radiated by the fire occurring within an area.'@en
rdfs:label: Fire radiative power

dct:description: 'Temperature of the fire occurring within an area.'@en
rdfs:label: Fire temperature

dct:description: 'Temperature of the apparent surface of land (bare soil or vegetation).'@en
rdfs:label: Land surface temperature

dct:description: 'Temperature of the lake surface.'@en
rdfs:label: Lake Surface Temperature

dct:description: 'Flux of carbon dioxide from the surface to the atmosphere'@en
rdfs:label: CO2 flux

dct:description: 'Total amount of vegetation in a reference area'@en
rdfs:label: Biomass

dct:description: 'Fraction of a land area where vegetation is present.'@en
rdfs:label: Fraction of vegetated land

dct:description: 'LAI (Leaf Area Index, LAI) is the total one-sided area of photosynthetic tissue per unit ground surface area.'@en
rdfs:label: Leaf Area Index (LAI)

dct:description: 'Difference between maximum (in NIR) and minimum (around the Red) vegetation reflectance, normalised to the summation. Representative of total biomass, supportive for computing LAI if not directly measured.'@en
rdfs:label: Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI)

dct:description: 'Result of the classification of different types of vegetation within a vegetated area - Accuracy expressed as inverse of the number of classes, so that smaller figures correspond to better performance.'@en
rdfs:label: Vegetation type

dct:description: 'Quantity of water evaporated from the soil and plants when the ground is at its natural moisture content.'@en
rdfs:label: Evaporation

dct:description: 'Fractional content of water in a volume of wet soil. Typically in a layer from the surface down to approximately 3 meters.'@en
rdfs:label: Soil moisture (in the roots region)

dct:description: 'Fractional content of water in a volume of wet soil. Surface layer (upper few centimetres).'@en
rdfs:label: Soil moisture at surface

dct:description: 'Fraction of PAR absorbed by vegetation (land or marine) for photosynthesis processes (generally around the 'red' frequencies).'@en
rdfs:label: Fraction of Absorbed PAR (FAPAR)

dct:description: 'Flux of downwelling photons of wavelength 400-700 nm.'@en
rdfs:label: Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR)

dct:description: 'The standard depths for soil temperature measurements are 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100 cm below the surface; additional depths may be included. The site for such measurements should be a level plot of bare ground (about 75 cm^2 ) and typical of the surrounding soil for which information is required.'@en
rdfs:label: Soil temperature

dct:description: 'Fraction of a land area covered by permanent ice.'@en
rdfs:label: Glacier cover

dct:description: 'Velocity of the ice measured at the surface of a glacier.'@en
rdfs:label: Glacier motion

dct:description: 'Map of the height of the glacier surface.'@en
rdfs:label: Glacier topography

dct:description: 'Map of ice sheet height over land.'@en
rdfs:label: Ice sheet topography

dct:description: 'The vertical depth of freshly fallen snow that has accumulated during a specific period.'@en
rdfs:label: Depth of snowfall

dct:description: 'The area of snow-covered ground, ice, or firn based on the fractional threshold used to define presence of snow.'@en
rdfs:label: Snow cover extent

dct:description: 'Vertical distance from the snow surface to a stated reference level.'@en
rdfs:label: Snow depth

dct:description: 'Binary product (dry or wet) expressing the presence of liquid water at the surface of the snow cover.'@en
rdfs:label: Snow surface state

dct:description: 'The Vertical depth of the water that would be obtained if the snow cover melted completely, which equates to the snow-cover mass per unit area.'@en
rdfs:label: Water equivalent of snow cover

dct:description: 'Vertical distance between the bottom of the ice and the top lake ice surface, excluding snow on ice.'@en
rdfs:label: Lake ice thickness

dct:description: 'Vertical distance between the bottom of the ice and the top river-ice surface, excluding snow on ice.'@en
rdfs:label: River ice thickness
